title: Collections: array versus `ArrayList`, and when each one fits

videos.script: Lesson 9's arrays have one fixed size, chosen the moment you create them. A library's list of loans does not know its size in advance. {{arraylist}} ArrayList is the answer most Java code reaches for: a list that grows as you add to it. This lesson starts with its everyday methods, and one trap with a list of numbers, where remove does something you did not ask for. {{growth}} Then a look inside. An ArrayList is an array, and when the array is full it is replaced by a bigger one. You will watch the size it picks, step by step. And you will see why adding at the front of a long list is so much slower than adding at the end. {{choosing}} Last, the choice. An array where the size is fixed and the values are primitives. A list everywhere else. And two lists that look ordinary and refuse to change. By the end you can pick between them for a reason.
